Owner login, admin login, tenant isolation, products CRUD/search/sort/pagination/promo validation/duplicate/bulk, categories CRUD/reorder/delete-with-target, store profile/appearance/delivery(fee=R$8 forced)/payments (both validations), status publish, media upload+fetch, share QR (PNG), invite flow + editor RBAC restriction (invite editor cannot invite), public catalog reflects appearance color and published products, analytics events + KPIs, admin overview counts (1 store, 16 products), admin stores list, plan change with invalid-plan 400, extend trial, suspend/reactivate + audit log. critical.issue: Lockout after 5 failed attempts does NOT trigger 429 behind Kubernetes ingress. Root cause: _brute_locked uses identifier = f'{ip}:{email}' with request.client.host, which returns the internal K8s pod IP (e.g. 10.208.147.130, 10.208.147.133). Requests are load-balanced across multiple pod replicas and each pod gets a different upstream hop IP, so counters get scattered and never reach the 5 threshold. Verified by inspecting login_attempts collection: two separate records with count=4 and count=3 for the same email across two ingress hops after 7 attempts. This means the feature is effectively bypassable in production. Fix: honor X-Forwarded-For (last trusted) or key the lockout purely on email (with a small per-IP secondary key), and/or use starlette's ProxyHeadersMiddleware / trust_hosts.

minor.issue: app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_credentials=True, allow_origins=['*']). Combining credentials with wildcard origins is invalid per CORS spec and modern browsers will reject cross-site cookie requests. Currently works only because the frontend and backend share the same origin via the ingress. Set CORS_ORIGINS explicitly to the FRONTEND_URL.
FastAPI @app.on_event is deprecated in favor of lifespan handlers (non-blocking).
Accept raw dict body without Pydantic validation of structure/keys — a malformed appearance object could overwrite store settings unpredictably.

issues: Renders correctly with hero image, categories, cart panel, checkout modal. All expected data-testids present (catalog-add-*, catalog-checkout, checkout-delivery/pickup/send).

action_items: HIGH: Fix brute-force lockout to work behind K8s ingress — use X-Forwarded-For or key the counter on email (not ip:email) and enable a proxy-headers middleware so request.client.host reflects the real client.
Restrict CORS_ORIGINS to the actual FRONTEND_URL when allow_credentials=True (spec compliance).
Optionally add Pydantic models for /store/appearance, /store/delivery, /store/payments bodies for stronger validation.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 930 lines — consider splitting into routers (auth, store, products, categories, admin, public).

Multiple endpoints (e.g. /categories/{cid}, /users/{uid}/*) use get_store_user (any store member) where owner/admin-only via require_store_manage would be safer for edit/delete actions. Editor role can currently delete/edit categories and products.
PUT /users/{uid}/role and DELETE /users/{uid} do not prevent demoting/removing the sole owner other than 'role != owner' guard on delete; role change can still convert owner to editor.
Time comparison uses ISO strings (e.g. locked_until, expires_at) — string comparison works for UTC ISO but is fragile; prefer storing datetimes.

rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout bug: FastAPI request.client.host returns the immediate upstream IP. In this Kubernetes environment the app sits behind an ingress + service that load-balances across pod replicas; each pod records a different internal hop IP as the client. Because the login_attempts identifier is 'ip:email', the same real user's 6 attempts land against 2–3 different identifiers, none of which reach count>=5. Reproduction: run 6 sequential POST /api/auth/login with a bad password for any email — all return 401 (never 429). Verified via `db.login_attempts.find({email: ...})` showing multiple docs with different '10.208.x.x:email' identifiers. Mitigation: (a) add Starlette's ProxyHeadersMiddleware / uvicorn --proxy-headers so request.client reflects X-Forwarded-For, or (b) drop IP from the identifier and use email only (with a global-per-email counter and optional per-IP secondary counter for defense-in-depth).
